first.rationale: The competitive threat of aggressive entry pricing targeting price-sensitive SMBs creates immediate revenue risk. Memory_73 demonstrates promotional pricing is effective for SMB acquisition and revenue in this segment. While activation and onboarding completion are both down 4-6% QoQ, the concurrent competitor entry makes pricing defense a higher priority than internal optimization. Verifying memory_73 (pricing effectiveness) and memory_31 (onboarding simplification baseline) will clarify whether a pricing intervention can be executed cleanly without confounding signals from the activation decline. A standard experiment allows calibrated pricing response without overcommitting. This preserves the option to address activation and onboarding if pricing stabilizes the segment, while directly countering the stated competitive threat. Long-term qualified revenue is protected by acting on proven SMB acquisition levers rather than pursuing uncertain activation improvements under pressure.
